source: NCERT Class XII, An Introduction to Indian Art (Part 2), Ch. 1 (The Manuscript Painting Tradition).

sections.heading: 1. Manuscript (Miniature) Painting
points: **Miniature paintings** = small, detailed paintings, often illustrating **manuscripts (books)**.
Early manuscripts were on **palm-leaf** and later **paper**; illustrations accompanied religious and literary texts.
Two early regional traditions: the **Pala school (eastern India)** and the **Western Indian (Jain) school**.

sections.heading: 2. The Pala School (Eastern India)
points: Flourished under the **Pala dynasty (Bihar/Bengal, 9th–12th c.)**; **Buddhist** manuscripts (on palm leaf), e.g. **Ashtasahasrika Prajnaparamita**.
Style: **graceful, flowing lines, gentle colours**; linked to the **Nalanda/Vikramshila** monasteries.
Influenced Buddhist art in Nepal, Tibet and Southeast Asia; declined with the fall of Buddhism in the region.

sections.heading: 3. The Western Indian / Jain School
points: Flourished in **Gujarat, Rajasthan, Malwa (11th–15th c.)**; illustrated **Jain texts** like the **Kalpasutra and Kalakacharya Katha**.
Style: **angular figures, the 'farther eye' projecting beyond the face**, bold colours (red, gold), stylised forms.
First on **palm leaf**, later on **paper**; use of **gold and ultramarine (lapis)** in later works.

sections.heading: 4. Transition to Later Schools
points: The manuscript tradition laid the foundation for later **miniature schools** (Rajasthani, Mughal, Deccan, Pahari).
The shift from palm leaf to **paper** allowed larger, more detailed paintings.
The **Sultanate period** saw a blending of Persian and Indian styles (e.g. Ni'mat-nama, Chaurapanchasika group).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Miniatures = small detailed paintings illustrating manuscripts.
Pala school (eastern India) = Buddhist palm-leaf manuscripts (Ashtasahasrika Prajnaparamita).
Western Indian/Jain school = Kalpasutra, Kalakacharya Katha; 'farther eye' projecting; angular figures.
Shift from palm leaf to paper enabled richer miniatures.
These traditions preceded Rajasthani, Mughal, Deccan and Pahari schools.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **Pala school = Buddhist** manuscripts (eastern India, palm-leaf).
The **Western Indian/Jain school** illustrated the **Kalpasutra**; noted for the **'farther eye'** convention.
Early manuscripts were on **palm leaf**, later on **paper**.
**Miniatures** are small paintings, usually illustrating books/manuscripts.
